subject: CB73A56CDCC6E0484B0C8324B42C7E3D
introduction: “The man who makes a piece of notepaper to the best of his ability, conscientiously, concentrating all his forces on perfecting it, is giving praise to God.” Bahá’u’lláh raised work done in a spirit of service to the rank of worship, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá said so to every carpenter, tailor, doctor and artist who wrote to him. The guide’s hundred passages make the one point. Paul the tentmaker and his “heartily, as to the Lord”, Ben Sira’s craftsmen who “maintain the state of the world”, Bezaleel, Herbert’s servant sweeping a room and the Gítá’s action without attachment to its fruit are the tradition. Genesis’s sweat, Mary’s better part and Thoreau’s quiet desperation are the three objections: work as curse, work as distraction, work as misery.
questions: What conditions do the readings attach to work’s being worship? Would any job qualify?
Martha worked and Mary listened. How do the readings change the terms of that story?
What turns work into “quiet desperation”, and can the worker’s own spirit change it?
If work is worship, what becomes of rest?

outside.why: It is incumbent on each to engage in some occupation. Study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands.
The man who makes a piece of notepaper to the best of his ability is giving praise to God. Herbert: who sweeps a room as for Thy laws makes that and the action fine.
Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.
Crafts and sciences which cause progress. Ben Sira on the smith and the potter: they will maintain the state of the world, and their desire is in the work of their craft.
In this age art is worship. Bezaleel was filled with the spirit of God, in all manner of workmanship.
Trade and profession conducted with trustworthiness. Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings.
One of the names of God is the Fashioner, and He loves craftsmanship. My Father worketh hitherto, and I work.
The purpose of knowledge is the benefit of God’s servants. Let him labour, that he may have to give to him that needeth.
Occupation in a craft is itself regarded as worship. Paul abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.

Martha was cumbered about much serving, and was told: Mary hath chosen that good part. The contemplative tradition took this as its charter. How do the readings answer it, and do they leave Mary anything?
Whoever earns his livelihood by his craft. Thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands: happy shalt thou be.

The craft of every craftsman is accounted as worship, “among the great favours”. Genesis calls labour the penalty: in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread. What has to be true of a job for the reading’s description to fit it better than Genesis’s?
Art or profession identical with worship. Carlyle: do the duty which lies nearest thee.
Occupation and labour are devotion. The Gítá: let right deeds be thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.
A day’s work done in the spirit of service. George Eliot: the growing good of the world is partly dependent on unhistoric acts.
Thoreau looked at working people and saw something else: the mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation. What makes the same day’s work worship for one person and desperation for another?
A believer engaged in his trade. Establish thou the work of our hands upon us.

shortfall: Eighty further readings repeat the principle to particular craftsmen, merchants and physicians.
